source "https://rubygems.org"
git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

ruby "3.3.6"

# Bundle edge Rails instead: gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
gem "rails", "7.0.8.7"
gem "concurrent-ruby", "1.3.4"

# The original asset pipeline for Rails [https://github.com/rails/sprockets-rails]
gem "sprockets-rails"

# Use postgresql as the database for Active Record
gem "pg", "1.6.0"

# Use the Puma web server [https://github.com/puma/puma]
gem "puma", "~> 5.0"

# Use JavaScript with ESM import maps [https://github.com/rails/importmap-rails]
gem "importmap-rails"

# Hotwire's SPA-like page accelerator [https://turbo.hotwired.dev]
gem "turbo-rails"

# Hotwire's modest JavaScript framework [https://stimulus.hotwired.dev]
gem "stimulus-rails"

# Build JSON APIs with ease [https://github.com/rails/jbuilder]
gem "jbuilder"

# Paginate the note list [https://github.com/ddnexus/pagy]
gem "pagy", "8.6.3"

# Run Active Job on Redis through Sidekiq [https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq]
gem "sidekiq", "6.5.12"
gem "redis", "4.8.1"

# Request citation metadata over HTTP [https://github.com/lostisland/faraday]
gem "faraday", "1.10.4"

# Use Kredis to get higher-level data types in Redis [https://github.com/rails/kredis]
# gem "kredis"

# Use Active Model has_secure_password [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_model_basics.html#securepassword]
gem "bcrypt", "~> 3.1.7"

# Windows does not include zoneinfo files, so bundle the tzinfo-data gem
gem "tzinfo-data", platforms: %i[ mingw mswin x64_mingw jruby ]

# Reduces boot times through caching; required in config/boot.rb
gem "bootsnap", require: false

# Use Sass to process CSS
# gem "sassc-rails"

# Use Active Storage variants [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#transforming-images]
# gem "image_processing", "~> 1.2"

group :development, :test do
  # See https://guides.rubyonrails.org/debugging_rails_applications.html#debugging-with-the-debug-gem
  gem "debug", platforms: %i[ mri mingw x64_mingw ]
end

group :development do
  # Use console on exceptions pages [https://github.com/rails/web-console]
  gem "web-console"

  # Add speed badges [https://github.com/MiniProfiler/rack-mini-profiler]
  # gem "rack-mini-profiler"

  # Speed up commands on slow machines / big apps [https://github.com/rails/spring]
  # gem "spring"
end

group :test do
  # Use system testing [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/testing.html#system-testing]
  gem "capybara"
  gem "selenium-webdriver"

  # Rails 7.0's test runner is incompatible with Minitest 6
  gem "minitest", "~> 5.25"
end

content.content:
# Architecture

## Starting point

Margin Notes is a reading-notebook application. Implemented so far:

- A reader (`User`) signs in with email and password through `has_secure_password`.
  `SessionsController` stores only the user ID in the Rails session.
  `ApplicationController#require_sign_in` protects the application's other
  controllers, but not Rails' Active Storage controllers.
- A reader owns `Notebook`s, and each `Note` belongs to one notebook. A note's
  owner is its notebook's owner, so `User#notes` (through notebooks) is the
  authorized note scope. There is no separate `user_id` on notes.
- `NotesController#index` serves `/notes` and its `/journal` alias. It lists the
  reader's notes newest first with an ID tie-breaker, and supports title search
  and notebook and status filters. `show` renders one note's rich body.
- Pagy 8.6.3 paginates that filtered list after ordering, 10 notes per page by
  default. The search form offers 5, 10, 25, or 50 as the `per_page` URL
  parameter. Larger requested sizes are capped at 50. Next and previous links keep
  the filters and page size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric page shows the
  first page, and a page past the end shows the last page. The form never sends
  an invalid size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric `per_page` in a URL is
  not handled, and Pagy raises `Pagy::VariableError`.
- A note's body is Action Text (`has_rich_text :body`), edited with Trix.
  Attachments are Active Storage blobs on the local Disk service. `Note` rejects
  saves that embed a blob over 1 MB. Direct uploads store blobs before this
  validation, without a size limit. Rejected or abandoned uploads remain
  unattached, and nothing purges them. No image processor is installed, so images
  use the original blobs, not variants. A migration converted existing plain-text
  bodies to escaped rich text.
- Action Text sanitizes rich text when it renders. The
  [Action Text initializer](config/initializers/action_text.rb) adds
  `details`/`summary` to the default allowlist for collapsible excerpts. Trix
  does not support those elements. Stored excerpts render as collapsible content,
  but saving them through the editor permanently flattens that structure, even
  when only tags or highlight change.
- Note tags are a JSON array in a text column, entered as a comma-separated
  list (`Note#tag_list`). The highlight color is `color` in the `settings` jsonb
  column, which the form edits as `highlight_color`.
- `NotebooksController#edit`/`update` are notebook settings. The slug is derived
  from the name on creation and is read-only afterward (`attr_readonly`). The
  settings form resubmits it unchanged. The export heading is stored in the
  serialized `preferences` hash. Markdown exports use both.
- A reader imports a CSV into one owned notebook. `ImportPreviewsController`
  reads the upload and renders a preview without saving. The preview page sends
  the CSV text back in a hidden field, and `ImportsController#create` reads and
  validates it again rather than trusting the preview. `Import#apply` saves the
  import and each row's note in one transaction. If any row cannot be saved,
  nothing from the batch remains. The receipt page and its CSV download list
  each imported note's title and DOI. Submitting the same preview twice creates
  two imports.
- `Import` accepts one format: UTF-8 CSV with the header row
  `title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch`, at most 100 notes and 100 KB.
  Only the title is required. Previews identify rows by their source line, so a
  quoted multi-line body keeps the line where its row starts. Body HTML takes the
  same Action Text assignment and render-time sanitization as the editor.
- A `Citation` is identified by its DOI, the table's `doi` primary key, and is
  shared by every reader who cites it. A DOI is stored as given apart from
  surrounding whitespace, so case variants are different citations. Rows in one
  import share a new citation. Two simultaneous imports that introduce the same
  new DOI can conflict; the losing request fails with a server error and saves
  nothing. A reader's annotation and optional reminder epoch belong to the note,
  not the citation. Annotations are plain text in both the preview and note page;
  line breaks are preserved on the note page, but markup is displayed literally.
  Applying an import does not schedule its reminders; the reader schedules each
  one from its note.
- A reader can also enter a DOI on the note form (`Note#doi=`), which cites the
  shared citation with that exact, trimmed DOI or creates it.
- A reader requests metadata for the citation on one of their notes with
  `CitationEnrichmentsController#create`, nested under the note. It resolves the
  note through `current_user.notes`, so another reader's note, or a note without
  a DOI, is a 404. `Citation#request_enrichment` marks the citation pending and
  queues `CitationEnrichmentJob`, unless a request is already pending. The job
  calls `Citation#enrich`, which stores the provider's title and source URL and
  marks the citation completed, or records a failure message. Metadata and
  status belong to the shared citation, so every note citing the DOI shows them.
  The note page shows the state; it does not update itself while pending.
- `Citation::Provider` is the HTTP client for the metadata provider. It reads
  its URL and basic-auth credentials from [config/secrets.yml](config/secrets.yml)
  through `Rails.application.secrets`; that file reads them from the environment.
  Faraday retries a GET once on 503. A 401, 403, or 404, or a response without a
  title and an http(s) URL, fails the enrichment at once. A 429 or 5xx, timeout,
  or connection failure raises `Citation::Provider::Unavailable`. The job retries
  that with `retry_on`, three attempts in all at exponentially longer waits, then
  records the failure instead of passing the error to Sidekiq's own retries. A
  persistently unavailable provider therefore receives at most six requests per
  enrichment request. A job that fails for another reason uses Sidekiq's retries
  and leaves the citation pending meanwhile.
- [bin/citation-provider](bin/citation-provider) is a deterministic local stand-in
  for the provider, used for development and demonstrations. No real provider or
  credentials are configured.
- A reader exports an owned notebook as Markdown from its exports page
  (`ExportsController`, nested under the notebook). `Notebook#request_export`
  saves a queued `Export`, then queues the native Sidekiq job `ExportJob` and
  stores its job ID, which the page shows. The export is committed before the
  job is queued so the worker can always load it. If Redis refuses the job, the
  export is removed and the request fails. Each request creates a new export.
- `Export#generate`, run by the worker, marks the export working with the
  notebook's note count, then writes the notes oldest first (creation time, then
  ID). The file starts with the notebook's export heading, or its name when none
  is set. Each note is a second-level heading with its title on one line,
  followed by its body as Action Text plain text. Markdown characters are not
  escaped. Progress is saved after each note. A retried job starts again from
  the first note. There is no failed state: while Sidekiq retries a failing job,
  the export shows as working and the reader can cancel it.
- Cancelling (`ExportCancellationsController`) sets a queued or working export's
  persisted status to cancelled under its row lock. The worker checks that status
  before each note and before completing, then stops and keeps no file. Completed
  and cancelled exports cannot be cancelled.
- The worker uploads the file to Active Storage (`<slug>.md`) before marking the
  export completed, so a completed export always has a file. It can be downloaded
  for 24 hours (`Export::AVAILABLE_FOR`). `ExportDownloadsController` resolves the
  export through the reader's notebook, so another reader's export is a 404, and
  checks `Export#downloadable?` on every request before any conditional response.
  An expired, cancelled, or unfinished export redirects to the exports page. The
  file is sent by the application, never by an Active Storage URL, with an ETag
  and Last-Modified from the stored file and `private, must-revalidate`.
  A failed upload can leave an unattached blob row without a stored file. Nothing
  cleans up those rows, and each failed retry can leave another one.
- The exports page caches each completed export's availability indicator as a
  fragment that expires at the export's deadline. The download action does not
  read that cache. The page does not update itself while an export is queued or
  working. Nothing purges expired files; they remain in storage.
- A notebook's activity page (`ActivityReportsController#show`, nested under the
  notebook and linked from the notebooks list) shows how many of its notes were
  created on each UTC date, newest date first. It is read-only and resolves the
  notebook through `current_user.notebooks`, so another reader's notebook is a
  404. `Notebook#daily_note_counts` groups the notes by `DATE(created_at)` in
  PostgreSQL and reads the rows with a raw `select_rows`, which returns each date
  as ISO 8601 text; the method parses it with `Date.iso8601`. Every status counts,
  and dates without notes are omitted. The report is derived from the notes that
  exist when it is requested, not an activity log: deleting a note lowers its
  date's count, and nothing records past counts.
- Each reader has a time zone (`User#time_zone`, UTC by default), chosen on the
  account settings page (`AccountsController`). Reminder times use it. Digests
  follow UTC days, and other pages still show times in UTC.
- A note's reminder is its `reminder_epoch`, a time in seconds since 1970, set by
  an import or by the reader. `RemindersController#create`, nested under the
  note, reads a date and time the reader entered in their time zone
  (`User#local_time`), or, with none, uses the stored time. `Note#schedule_reminder`
  queues `NoteReminderJob` for that time with `set(wait_until:)` and stores the
  job's ID, under the note's row lock, so a failed enqueue keeps the earlier
  reminder. A local time that does not exist because of a daylight saving change
  moves forward, and an ambiguous one takes its first occurrence. A time in the
  past is sent as soon as a worker runs the job.
- Scheduling again, or postponing (`ReminderPostponementsController`), replaces the
  reminder. Earlier jobs stay in Sidekiq's schedule, but send nothing: when a job
  runs, `Note#send_reminder` takes the row lock and emails the reader only if its
  job ID is still the note's and the reminder has not been sent, then records
  `reminder_sent_at`. The note page shows whether a reminder is imported but not
  scheduled, scheduled, or sent. A job that fails after the email is written can
  send it again when Sidekiq retries it.
- Postponing moves the reminder 24 elapsed hours later. The note page previews
  that time as `reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`, which keeps the reminder's UTC
  offset. Across a daylight saving change the preview shows the right instant,
  but at a different offset and wall-clock time from the postponed reminder.
- A reader requests a digest of their ready notes from the notes page
  (`DigestsController`). `User#request_digest` reserves the reader's ID in a
  Redis set for the request's UTC date
  (`digest_requests:YYYY-MM-DD`, kept for two days) and queues `DigestJob` with
  the reader, the request time in the reader's zone, and the share of their notes
  that are ready, as a `BigDecimal`. A reader whose ID is already in the day's set
  is told the digest was already requested. If the job cannot be queued, the
  reservation is removed and the error raised, so the request fails and can be
  repeated. The reservation prevents repeated requests, not repeated emails:
  Sidekiq can run a job more than once. Each request logs redis-rb's deprecation
  warning for a single-member `sadd`, and Sidekiq warns that the job's arguments
  are not native JSON types, because of the `BigDecimal`.
- Sidekiq stores the job's arguments as JSON. Active Job 7.0 sends the request
  time with its UTC offset but deserializes it in the worker's zone, UTC, and the
  completion arrives as a decimal string such as `"0.6667"`. `DigestMailer` lists
  the reader's ready notes last updated during that UTC day, and dates the digest
  by it. The content day matches the reservation's day, even near local midnight.
  A digest is a snapshot when its job runs; notes updated afterward are not sent
  in a second digest for that UTC day.
- The mailers write plain-text email. Development writes each recipient's email
  to `tmp/mails` (Action Mailer's file delivery); tests use the `:test` delivery
  method. Production has no delivery method or link host configured.
- Active Storage serves blobs through signed URLs from its own controllers. Those
  URLs are not checked against the signed-in reader. The embedded blob redirect
  URLs do not expire, although the Disk-service URLs they redirect to do.
  The direct-upload controller checks CSRF, not sign-in; the public sign-in page
  supplies a CSRF token to anonymous clients. This sample has no private-file
  access policy or upload-abuse protection for a public deployment.

These conventions guide further features without prescribing a schema in advance.

The initial runtime is Ruby 3.3.6 and Rails 7.0.8.7 with Rails 7.0 defaults.
[Gemfile](Gemfile), [Gemfile.lock](Gemfile.lock), [.ruby-version](.ruby-version), and
[config/application.rb](config/application.rb) are the executable sources of truth.

- PostgreSQL is the application database. Use Active Record and migrations for
  application-owned records, constraints, indexes, and transactions.
- ERB renders HTML. The generated app includes Sprockets, importmap, Turbo, and
  Stimulus. Jbuilder is available for requested JSON representations, but an HTML
  feature does not automatically need a JSON API.
- Rails includes the mailer, job, storage, and cable frameworks. Their presence
  does not mean broadcasts are implemented features. Email is sent only for
  reminders and digests, and is not delivered outside development's files. File
  uploads exist only as rich-text attachments.
- Active Job uses Sidekiq 6.5 as its adapter outside tests, so queued jobs are
  kept in Redis (`REDIS_URL`, by default `redis://localhost:6379`) and run in a
  separate `bundle exec sidekiq` process. Tests use Active Job's test adapter.
  `ExportJob` is a native Sidekiq job rather than an Active Job, so its job ID can
  be shown. Sidekiq stores its arguments as JSON, and it uses Sidekiq's default
  retries.
- Action Text 7.0.8.7 bundles Trix 1.3.4. That version cannot load saved HTML
  that has attributes, such as links or attachments, so the layout loads Trix
  1.3.5 from `vendor/javascript` as a classic script. Trix 1.x is not an ES
  module, so it is not in the import map. `@rails/actiontext` is.
  The vendored build comes from the [Trix 1.3.5 release](https://github.com/basecamp/trix/tree/1.3.5)
  and includes its [MIT license](vendor/javascript/trix-1.3.5.LICENSE).
- Orb setup starts PostgreSQL and Redis. Redis holds Sidekiq's queues and the
  digest reservations; it is not an application cache. The generated production
  cable configuration names Redis. That configuration is not a verified deployment.

## Prefer Rails objects with clear responsibilities

Use the framework's ordinary directories and interfaces:

| Responsibility | Home |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP verbs, paths, and resource nesting | `config/routes.rb` |
| Parameter selection, authorized lookup, response negotiation | `app/controllers/` |
| Persistent state and domain operations | `app/models/` |
| A cohesive capability of one model | A namespace beneath `app/models/` |
| Behavior genuinely shared across models | `app/models/concerns/` |
| HTML, Turbo stream, and JSON representations | `app/views/` |
| Presentation helpers | `app/helpers/` |
| Browser interaction around rendered HTML | `app/javascript/controllers/` |
| Background execution and retry boundary | `app/jobs/` |
| Mail composition | `app/mailers/` and its views |

A controller can call Active Record directly for a simple save. A multi-step
domain transition belongs behind a meaningful model method, not a sequence of
unrelated updates in the controller. Use a plain Ruby object or Active Model when
an operation needs its own object but no database table. Do not introduce a
mandatory service, repository, presenter, or command layer between every pair of
Rails objects.

Fizzy models closing a card as a singular closure resource. Its controller calls
`Card#close`, and `Card::Closeable` owns the association, predicates, and transaction.
The [closure sources](docs/references/fizzy.md#card-closure) illustrate a resource
boundary and a domain method, not a requirement to add cards to Margin Notes.

## Model resources, not collections of verbs

Use the conventional REST actions, including `new` and `edit` for HTML forms.
When a new operation does not fit an existing resource, look for the resource it
creates, updates, or removes before adding a custom action. Keep nesting shallow
enough that the parent conveys ownership rather than reproducing the whole schema.

Use route helpers in views and responses. Controllers choose the representation.
Models do not construct controller responses or reach into request parameters.

## Keep data ownership and effects explicit

- PostgreSQL owns durable application facts. Derive a value from those facts
  unless storing it solves a demonstrated query, history, or concurrency need.
- Put invariants used outside HTTP in the domain model. Add database constraints
  when integrity must also hold across concurrent requests and non-model writes.
- Keep related database writes in one transaction. Do not assume it can undo a
  remote request, an email, or a job already sent to another system.
- Jobs should delegate to domain behavior and carry the identifiers or context
  they need. Decide retries, duplicate delivery, and transaction timing when a
  real background feature is introduced, rather than adding a queue preemptively.
- Keep network clients at visible boundaries. Preserve failure information and
  distinguish a legitimate empty response from a failed operation.

Fizzy's [comment example](docs/references/fizzy.md#comments) enforces comment
eligibility in both the model and the controller. Callers outside HTTP must obey
the same rule.

## Authorization is not presentation

Define ownership and the authorized lookup scope together. Resolve records
through the signed-in reader: `current_user.notebooks` and `current_user.notes`.
Direct lookups outside that scope raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, which is
a 404 in production. A submitted `notebook_id` is resolved through
`current_user.notebooks.find_by`, never assigned directly. A missing or foreign
notebook fails validation and renders the form with 422, without saving the note.
Resolve nested records through their authorized parent. Neither an unguessable ID
nor a hidden or disabled button grants or checks permission.

Keep actor-dependent decisions explicit in domain APIs and reusable rendering.
If request-local state is introduced, set and reset it at the request boundary.
Jobs, mailers, and tests must not rely on a previous request having populated it.
Do not adopt a tenancy or identity scheme solely because a reference application
uses one.

## Render on the server, enhance in the browser

Use HTML forms and links for their native semantics. Turbo handles navigation,
frames, and targeted replacements. Stimulus supplies local interaction that HTML
does not provide. Keep persistence and authorization on the server, not in a
second client-side model of the domain.

Partials take the resources and presentation inputs they need. A template may
compose several resources. A reusable partial should not depend on a particular
controller's incidental instance variables or on undeclared request context.
See the [view guide](docs/guides/views.md) for HTML, accessibility, Turbo, and JSON.

## Optimize the actual representation

Start with correct queries and clear response contracts. Filter and order before
pagination. Use a stable tie-breaker where page membership must be deterministic.
Load the associations that the rendered representation uses rather than adding
a universal preload list to every request.

Define cache keys and invalidation rules before introducing caching. Include
permissions, locale, and related-record changes when they affect the output, or
keep those parts outside the shared fragment. The
[board example](docs/references/fizzy.md#boards-and-caching) illustrates why a
warm cache must be tested with another viewer, not just the same request twice.

## Scope and reference boundaries

The [public examples](docs/references/fizzy.md) are evidence for design ideas, not
a compatible application template. Their Ruby, Rails, database adapters, asset
pipeline, editors, and helper libraries differ from this repository. Use the
locked local APIs, and introduce new infrastructure only for a requested feature.

As features land, document their ownership and invariants here. Keep detailed
layer practices in the [model](docs/guides/models.md),
[controller](docs/guides/controllers.md), and [view](docs/guides/views.md) guides,
and verification rules in [TESTING.md](TESTING.md).

def serialize(attr_name, coder: nil, type: Object, comparable: false, yaml: {}, **options)
          coder ||= default_column_serializer
          unless coder
            raise ArgumentError, <<~MSG.squish
              missing keyword: :coder

              If no default coder is configured, a coder must be provided to `serialize`.
            MSG
          end

          column_serializer = build_column_serializer(attr_name, coder, type, yaml)

          attribute(attr_name, **options)

          decorate_attributes([attr_name]) do |attr_name, cast_type|
            if type_incompatible_with_serialize?(cast_type, coder, type)
              raise ColumnNotSerializableError.new(attr_name, cast_type)
            end

            cast_type = cast_type.subtype if Type::Serialized === cast_type
            Type::Serialized.new(cast_type, column_serializer, comparable: comparable)
          end
        end

        # To introduce a change in behavior, follow these steps:
        # 1. Add an accessor on the target object (e.g. the ActiveJob class for
        #    global Active Job config).

        #    applications.
        # 3. Implement the behavior change based on the config value.
        # 4. In the section below corresponding to the next release of Rails,

        # 5. Add a commented out section in the `new_framework_defaults` to
        #    configure the default value again.
        # 6. Update the guide in `configuring.md`.

        # 1. Update or remove the entry in the guides.

        # Merges the default options with ones specific to a method call.
        def merged_options(call_options)
          if call_options
            call_options = normalize_options(call_options)
            if call_options.key?(:expires_in) && call_options.key?(:expires_at)
              raise ArgumentError, "Either :expires_in or :expires_at can be supplied, but not both"
            end

            expires_at = call_options.delete(:expires_at)
            call_options[:expires_in] = (expires_at - Time.now) if expires_at

            if call_options[:expires_in].is_a?(Time)
              expires_in = call_options[:expires_in]
              raise ArgumentError.new("expires_in parameter should not be a Time. Did you mean to use expires_at? Got: #{expires_in}")
            end
            if call_options[:expires_in]&.negative?

              handle_invalid_expires_in("Cache expiration time is invalid, cannot be negative: #{expires_in}")

            if options.empty?
              call_options
            else
              options.merge(call_options)
            end
          else
            options

        end

def retry_on(*exceptions, wait: 3.seconds, attempts: 5, queue: nil, priority: nil, jitter: JITTER_DEFAULT, report: false)
        rescue_from(*exceptions) do |error|
          executions = executions_for(exceptions)
          if attempts == :unlimited || executions < attempts
            ActiveSupport.error_reporter.report(error, source: "application.active_job") if report
            retry_job wait: determine_delay(seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm: wait, executions: executions, jitter: jitter), queue: queue, priority: priority, error: error
          else
            if block_given?
              instrument :retry_stopped, error: error do
                yield self, error
              end
              run_after_discard_procs(error)
            else
              instrument :retry_stopped, error: error
              run_after_discard_procs(error)
              raise error
            end
          end
        end
      def determine_delay(seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm:, executions:, jitter: JITTER_DEFAULT)
        jitter = jitter == JITTER_DEFAULT ? self.class.retry_jitter : (jitter || 0.0)

        case seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm
        when :exponentially_longer
          delay = executions**4
          delay_jitter = determine_jitter_for_delay(delay, jitter)
          delay + delay_jitter + 2
        when ActiveSupport::Duration, Integer
          delay = seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm.to_i
          delay_jitter = determine_jitter_for_delay(delay, jitter)
          delay + delay_jitter
        when Proc
          algorithm = seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm
          algorithm.call(executions)
        else

## Rails 8.1.0 (October 22, 2025) ##

*   Add structured events for Active Job:
    - `active_job.enqueued`
    - `active_job.bulk_enqueued`
    - `active_job.started`
    - `active_job.completed`
    - `active_job.retry_scheduled`
    - `active_job.retry_stopped`
    - `active_job.discarded`
    - `active_job.interrupt`
    - `active_job.resume`
    - `active_job.step_skipped`
    - `active_job.step_started`
    - `active_job.step`

    *Adrianna Chang*

*   Deprecate built-in `sidekiq` adapter.

    If you're using this adapter, upgrade to `sidekiq` 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.

    *fatkodima*

*   Remove deprecated internal `SuckerPunch` adapter in favor of the adapter included with the `sucker_punch` gem.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove support to set `ActiveJob::Base.enqueue_after_transaction_commit` to `:never`, `:always` and `:default`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated `Rails.application.config.active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   `ActiveJob::Serializers::ObjectSerializers#klass` method is now public.

    Custom Active Job serializers must have a public `#klass` method too.
    The returned class will be index allowing for faster serialization.

    *Jean Boussier*

*   Allow jobs to the interrupted and resumed with Continuations

    A job can use Continuations by including the `ActiveJob::Continuable`
    concern. Continuations split jobs into steps. When the queuing system
    is shutting down jobs can be interrupted and their progress saved.

    ```ruby
    class ProcessImportJob
      include ActiveJob::Continuable

      def perform(import_id)
        @import = Import.find(import_id)

        # block format
        step :initialize do
          @import.initialize
        end

        # step with cursor, the cursor is saved when the job is interrupted
        step :process do |step|
          @import.records.find_each(start: step.cursor) do |record|
            record.process
            step.advance! from: record.id
          end
        end

        # method format
        step :finalize

        private
          def finalize
            @import.finalize
          end
      end
    end
    ```

    *Donal McBreen*

*   Defer invocation of ActiveJob enqueue callbacks until after commit when
    `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` is enabled.

    *Will Roever*

*   Add `report:` option to `ActiveJob::Base#retry_on` and `#discard_on`

    When the `report:` option is passed, errors will be reported to the error reporter
    before being retried / discarded.

    *Andrew Novoselac*

*   Accept a block for `ActiveJob::ConfiguredJob#perform_later`.

    This was inconsistent with a regular `ActiveJob::Base#perform_later`.

    *fatkodima*

*   Raise a more specific error during deserialization when a previously serialized job class is now unknown.

    `ActiveJob::UnknownJobClassError` will be raised instead of a more generic
    `NameError` to make it easily possible for adapters to tell if the `NameError`
    was raised during job execution or deserialization.

    *Earlopain*

## Rails 7.2.0 (August 09, 2024) ##

*   All tests now respect the `active_job.queue_adapter` config.

    Previously if you had set `config.active_job.queue_adapter` in your `config/application.rb`
    or `config/environments/test.rb` file, the adapter you selected was previously not used consistently
    across all tests. In some tests your adapter would be used, but other tests would use the `TestAdapter`.

    In Rails 7.2, all tests will respect the `queue_adapter` config if provided. If no config is provided,
    the `TestAdapter` will continue to be used.

    See [#48585](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/48585) for more details.

    *Alex Ghiculescu*

*   Make Active Job transaction aware when used conjointly with Active Record.

    A common mistake with Active Job is to enqueue jobs from inside a transaction,
    causing them to potentially be picked and ran by another process, before the
    transaction is committed, which may result in various errors.

    ```ruby
    Topic.transaction do
      topic = Topic.create(...)
      NewTopicNotificationJob.perform_later(topic)
    end
    ```

    Now Active Job will automatically defer the enqueuing to after the transaction is committed,
    and drop the job if the transaction is rolled back.

    Various queue implementations can choose to disable this behavior, and users can disable it,
    or force it on a per job basis:

    ```ruby
    class NewTopicNotificationJob < ApplicationJob
      self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = :never # or `:always` or `:default`
    end
    ```

    *Maxime Réty*

    *Joshua Young*

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated primitive serializer for `BigDecimal` arguments.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

gem "sidekiq", ">= 4.1.0"
require "sidekiq"

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # = Sidekiq adapter for Active Job
    #
    # Simple, efficient background processing for Ruby. Sidekiq uses threads to
    # handle many jobs at the same time in the same process. It does not
    # require \Rails but will integrate tightly with it to make background
    # processing dead simple.
    #
    # Read more about Sidekiq {here}[http://sidekiq.org].
    #
    # To use Sidekiq set the queue_adapter config to +:sidekiq+.
    #
    #   Rails.application.config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq
    class SidekiqAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      def initialize(*) # :nodoc:
        @stopping = false

        Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end

        Sidekiq.configure_client do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end
      end

      def check_adapter
        ActiveJob.deprecator.warn <<~MSG.squish
          The built-in `sidekiq` adapter is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 8.2.
          Please upgrade `sidekiq` gem to version 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.
        MSG
      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name
        ).perform_async(job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name,
        ).perform_at(timestamp, job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_all(jobs) # :nodoc:
        enqueued_count = 0
        jobs.group_by(&:class).each do |job_class, same_class_jobs|
          same_class_jobs.group_by(&:queue_name).each do |queue, same_class_and_queue_jobs|
            immediate_jobs, scheduled_jobs = same_class_and_queue_jobs.partition { |job| job.scheduled_at.nil? }

            if immediate_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => immediate_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end

            if scheduled_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
                "at" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| job.scheduled_at&.to_f }
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end
          end
        end
        enqueued_count
      end

      class JobWrapper # :nodoc:
        include Sidekiq::Worker

        def perform(job_data)
          Base.execute job_data.merge("provider_job_id" => jid)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

module ActiveJob
  module Serializers
    class TimeWithZoneSerializer < ObjectSerializer # :nodoc:
      NANO_PRECISION = 9

      def serialize(time_with_zone)
        super(
          "value" => time_with_zone.iso8601(NANO_PRECISION),
          "time_zone" => time_with_zone.time_zone.tzinfo.name
        )
      end

      def deserialize(hash)
        Time.iso8601(hash["value"]).in_time_zone(hash["time_zone"] || Time.zone)
      end

      def klass
        ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone
      end
    end
  end
end

        tags: sanitizer_allowed_tags,
        attributes: sanitizer_allowed_attributes,
        scrubber: scrubber,
      ).html_safe
    end

    def render_action_text_attachments(content)
      content.render_attachments do |attachment|
        unless attachment.in?(content.gallery_attachments)
          attachment.node.tap do |node|
            node.inner_html = render_action_text_attachment attachment, locals: { in_gallery: false }
          end
        end

            attachment.node.inner_html = render_action_text_attachment attachment, locals: { in_gallery: true }

          end.join.html_safe

      end
    end

Idle minds

,10.1000/Essays.1,Read twice & reflect,1767225600 "Of experience","

Long essay

",10.1000/Essays.1,Compare with Bacon, CSV assert_no_changes -> { record_counts } do post notebook_import_preview_path(notebook), params: { import: { file: upload(csv) } } end assert_response :success assert_select "#line_2 h2", "Line 2: On idleness" assert_select "#line_2 dd", "Read twice & reflect" assert_select "#line_4 h2", "Line 4: Of experience" assert_select "#line_4 dd", "Compare with Bacon" assert_select "#line_2 time[datetime=?]", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" csv_field = css_select("input[type=hidden][name='import[csv]']").first["value"] assert_difference -> { Note.count } => 2, -> { Citation.count } => 1, -> { Import.count } => 1 do post notebook_imports_path(notebook), params: { import: { csv: csv_field } } end import = Import.last assert_redirected_to notebook_import_path(notebook, import) idleness, experience = import.notes.order(:id) assert_equal [notebook, notebook], [idleness.notebook, experience.notebook] assert_equal ["Read twice & reflect", 1767225600], [idleness.annotation, idleness.reminder_epoch] assert_equal ["Compare with Bacon", nil], [experience.annotation, experience.reminder_epoch] get note_path(idleness) assert_select ".trix-content b", "minds" assert_select ".citation dd", text: "Read twice & reflect" get notebook_import_path(notebook, import, format: :csv) assert_equal "text/csv", response.media_type assert_equal "title,doi\nOn idleness,10.1000/Essays.1\nOf experience,10.1000/Essays.1\n", response.body end test "invalid rows are shown with their errors, and applying them saves nothing" do notebook = notebooks(:novels) csv = <<~CSV title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch Adam Bede,

def expand_from_hash(attributes, &block)
        return [Arel.sql("1=0", retryable: true)] if attributes.empty?

        attributes.flat_map do |key, value|
          if key.is_a?(Array) && key.size == 1
            key = key.first
            value = value.flatten
          end

          if key.is_a?(Array)
            queries = Array(value).map do |ids_set|
              raise ArgumentError, "Expected corresponding value for #{key} to be an Array" unless ids_set.is_a?(Array)
              expand_from_hash(key.zip(ids_set).to_h)
            end
            grouping_queries(queries)
          elsif value.is_a?(Hash) && !table.has_column?(key)
            table.associated_table(key, &block)
              .predicate_builder.expand_from_hash(value.stringify_keys)
          elsif (associated_reflection = table.associated_with(key))
            # Find the foreign key when using queries such as:
            # Post.where(author: author)
            #
            # For polymorphic relationships, find the foreign key and type:
            # PriceEstimate.where(estimate_of: treasure)

            if associated_reflection.polymorphic?
              value = [value] unless value.is_a?(Array)
              klass = PolymorphicArrayValue
            elsif associated_reflection.through_reflection?
              associated_table = table.associated_table(key)

              next associated_table.predicate_builder.expand_from_hash(
                associated_table.primary_key => value
              )
            end

            klass ||= AssociationQueryValue
            queries = klass.new(associated_reflection, value).queries.map! do |query|
              # If the query produced is identical to attributes don't go any deeper.
              # Prevents stack level too deep errors when association and foreign_key are identical.
              query == attributes ? self[key, value] : expand_from_hash(query)
            end

            grouping_queries(queries)
          elsif table.aggregated_with?(key)
            mapping = table.reflect_on_aggregation(key).mapping
            values = value.nil? ? [nil] : Array.wrap(value)
            if mapping.length == 1 || values.empty?
              column_name, aggr_attr = mapping.first
              values = values.map do |object|
                object.respond_to?(aggr_attr) ? object.public_send(aggr_attr) : object
              end
              self[column_name, values]
            else
              queries = values.map do |object|
                mapping.map do |field_attr, aggregate_attr|
                  self[field_attr, object.try!(aggregate_attr)]
                end
              end

              grouping_queries(queries)
            end
          else
            self[key, value]
          end
        end

    @to_time_preserves_timezone
  end

    def to_datetime
      @to_datetime ||= utc.to_datetime.new_offset(Rational(utc_offset, 86_400))

    # with the same UTC offset as +self+ or in the local system timezone

require "test_helper"
require "minitest/mock"

class DigestsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test "a reader can request one digest per UTC day, listing ready notes updated that day" do
    release_digest_reservations "2026-10-04", "2026-10-05", "2026-10-06"
    users(:reader).update!(time_zone: "Eastern Time (US & Canada)")
    notes(:montaigne).update_columns(updated_at: Time.utc(2026, 10, 4, 16))

    travel_to Time.utc(2026, 10, 5, 3, 30) do
      notebooks(:essays).notes.create!(title: "Bacon on studies", status: :ready)
      notebooks(:novels).notes.create!(title: "Adam Bede, unfinished", status: :draft)

      sign_in_as users(:reader)
      post digest_path
      assert_redirected_to notes_path
      assert_equal "Today's reading digest is on its way.", flash[:notice]

      travel 9.hours + 30.minutes
      post digest_path
      assert_equal "You have already requested today's reading digest.", flash[:notice]

      sign_in_as users(:other_reader)
      post digest_path
      assert_equal "Today's reading digest is on its way.", flash[:notice]
    end

    assert_equal [users(:reader), users(:other_reader)], enqueued_jobs.map { |job| GlobalID::Locator.locate(job[:args].first["_aj_globalid"]) }
    assert_equal "2026-10-04T23:30:00.000000000-04:00", enqueued_jobs.first[:args].second["value"], "the job carries the reader's local time"

    perform_enqueued_jobs
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.find { |delivery| delivery.to == ["reader@example.com"] }
    assert_equal "Your reading digest for October 05, 2026", mail.subject
    assert_includes mail.body.to_s, "- Bacon on studies (Essays)"
    assert_not_includes mail.body.to_s, "Montaigne"
    assert_not_includes mail.body.to_s, "Adam Bede"
    assert_includes mail.body.to_s, "50% of your notes were ready"

    travel_to Time.utc(2026, 10, 6, 0, 30) do
      sign_in_as users(:reader)
      assert_enqueued_jobs(1, only: DigestJob) { post digest_path }
    end
  end

  test "a digest request is released when its job cannot be queued" do
    release_digest_reservations "2026-10-07"
    sign_in_as users(:reader)

    travel_to Time.utc(2026, 10, 7, 12) do
      DigestJob.stub(:perform_later, ->(*) { raise Redis::CannotConnectError }) do
        assert_raises(Redis::CannotConnectError) { post digest_path }
      end
      assert_no_enqueued_jobs

      post digest_path
      assert_equal "Today's reading digest is on its way.", flash[:notice]
      assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: DigestJob
    end
  end

  private
    # Reservations are kept in Redis, outside the test database's transactions.
    def release_digest_reservations(*dates)
      readers = [users(:reader).id, users(:other_reader).id]
      Sidekiq.redis { |redis| dates.each { |date| redis.srem("digest_requests:#{date}", readers) } }
    end
end

def build_column_serializer(attr_name, coder, type, yaml = nil)
            # When ::JSON is used, force it to go through the Active Support JSON encoder
            # to ensure special objects (e.g. Active Record models) are dumped correctly
            # using the #as_json hook.

            if coder == ::JSON || coder == Coders::JSON
              coder = Coders::JSON.new
            end

            if coder == ::YAML || coder == Coders::YAMLColumn
              Coders::YAMLColumn.new(attr_name, type, **(yaml || {}))
            elsif coder.respond_to?(:new) && !coder.respond_to?(:load)
              coder.new(attr_name, type)
            elsif type && type != Object
              Coders::ColumnSerializer.new(attr_name, coder, type)
            else
              coder
            end
          end
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "active_support/json"

module ActiveRecord
  module Coders # :nodoc:
    class JSON # :nodoc:
      DEFAULT_OPTIONS = { escape: false }.freeze

      def initialize(options = nil)
        @options = options ? DEFAULT_OPTIONS.merge(options) : DEFAULT_OPTIONS
        @encoder = ActiveSupport::JSON::Encoding.json_encoder.new(options)
      end

      def dump(obj)
        @encoder.encode(obj)
      end

      def load(json)
        ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(json, @options) unless json.blank?
      end
    end
  end
end

def within_new_transaction(isolation: nil, joinable: true)
        isolation ||= @connection.pool.pool_transaction_isolation_level
        @connection.lock.synchronize do
          transaction = begin_transaction(isolation: isolation, joinable: joinable)
          begin
            yield transaction.user_transaction
          rescue Exception => error
            rollback_transaction
            after_failure_actions(transaction, error)

            raise
          ensure
            unless error
              if Thread.current.status == "aborting"
                rollback_transaction
              else
                begin
                  commit_transaction
                rescue ActiveRecord::ConnectionFailed
                  transaction.invalidate! unless transaction.state.completed?
                  raise
                rescue Exception
                  rollback_transaction(transaction) unless transaction.state.completed?
                  raise
                end
              end
            end
          end
        ensure
          unless transaction&.state&.completed?
            @connection.throw_away!
            transaction&.incomplete!
          end
        end
      end
=====7.0
      def within_new_transaction(isolation: nil, joinable: true)
        @connection.lock.synchronize do
          transaction = begin_transaction(isolation: isolation, joinable: joinable)
          ret = yield
          completed = true
          ret
        rescue Exception => error
          if transaction
            transaction.state.invalidate! if error.is_a? ActiveRecord::TransactionRollbackError
            rollback_transaction
            after_failure_actions(transaction, error)
          end

          raise
        ensure
          if transaction
            if error
              # @connection still holds an open or invalid transaction, so we must not
              # put it back in the pool for reuse.
              @connection.throw_away! unless transaction.state.rolledback?
            elsif Thread.current.status == "aborting" || (!completed && transaction.written)
              # The transaction is still open but the block returned earlier.
              #
              # The block could return early because of a timeout or because the thread is aborting,
              # so we are rolling back to make sure the timeout didn't caused the transaction to be
              # committed incompletely.
              rollback_transaction
            else
              begin
                commit_transaction
              rescue Exception
                rollback_transaction(transaction) unless transaction.state.completed?
                raise
              end
            end
          end
        end
      end

    *Haroon Ahmed*

*   Touch all corresponding model records after ActiveStorage::Blob is analyzed

    This fixes a race condition where a record can be requested and have a cache entry built, before
    the initial `analyze_later` completes, which will not be invalidated until something else
    updates the record. This also invalidates cache entries when a blob is re-analyzed, which
    is helpful if a bug is fixed in an analyzer or a new analyzer is added.

    *Nate Matykiewicz*

*   Add ability to use pre-defined variants when calling `preview` or
    `representation` on an attachment.

    ```ruby
    class User < ActiveRecord::Base
      has_one_attached :file do |attachable|
        attachable.variant :thumb, resize_to_limit: [100, 100]
      end
    end

    <%= image_tag user.file.representation(:thumb) %>
    ```

    *Richard Böhme*

*   Method `attach` always returns the attachments except when the record
    is persisted, unchanged, and saving it fails, in which case it returns `nil`.

    *Santiago Bartesaghi*

    ```ruby

        filename: "dummy.txt",

      user.attachments.attach({
## Rails 8.0.0.beta1 (September 26, 2024) ##

*   Deprecate `ActiveStorage::Service::AzureStorageService`.

    *zzak*

*   Improve `ActiveStorage::Filename#sanitized` method to handle special characters more effectively.
    Replace the characters `"*?<>` with `-` if they exist in the Filename to match the Filename convention of Win OS.

    *Luong Viet Dung(Martin)*

*   Improve InvariableError, UnpreviewableError and UnrepresentableError message.

    Include Blob ID and content_type in the messages.

    *Petrik de Heus*

    *Nate Matykiewicz*

    [CVE-2025-24293]

    *Zack Deveau*

## Rails 8.0.2 (March 12, 2025) ##

*   A Blob will no longer autosave associated Attachment.

    This fixes an issue where a record with an attachment would have
    its dirty attributes reset, preventing your `after commit` callbacks
    on that record to behave as expected.

    Note that this change doesn't require any changes on your application
    and is supposed to be internal. Active Storage Attachment will continue
    to be autosaved (through a different relation).

    *Edouard-chin*

    get note_path(note)
    assert_select "#citation_metadata", /Failed: The provider is unavailable \(HTTP 503\)/
    assert_select "#citation_metadata button", "Fetch again"

    end

    assert_equal "The provider rejected the configured credentials (HTTP 401)", note.citation.reload.enrichment_error
    assert_nil note.citation.title

    with_provider([200, { title: "Essais", url: "javascript:alert(1)" }]) do

    assert_equal ["failed", nil], [note.citation.reload.enrichment_status, note.citation.source_url]
    get note_path(note)

  end

  test "readers can only request metadata through their own cited notes" do
    other_note = notes(:other_secret)
    other_note.update!(doi: "10.1000/private")

    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound) { post note_citation_enrichment_path(other_note) }
    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound) { post note_citation_enrichment_path(notes(:montaigne)) }

    assert_nil other_note.citation.reload.enrichment_status
  end

  private
    # Serves the given [status, JSON] responses in order from a loopback HTTP
    # server, repeating the last, and returns each request's DOI and
    # Authorization header.
    def with_provider(*responses)
      requests = []
      app = lambda do |env|
        requests << [Rack::Request.new(env).params["doi"], env["HTTP_AUTHORIZATION"]]
        status, body = responses.size > 1 ? responses.shift : responses.first
        [status, { "Content-Type" => "application/json" }, [body.to_json]]
      end

      server = Puma::Server.new(app, Puma::Events.strings)
      server.add_tcp_listener("127.0.0.1", 0)
      server.run

      settings = Rails.application.secrets.citation_provider
      Rails.application.secrets.citation_provider = settings.merge(url: "http://127.0.0.1:#{server.connected_ports.first}")
      yield
      requests
    ensure
      Rails.application.secrets.citation_provider = settings if settings
      server&.stop(true)
    end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "sidekiq/job"

module Sidekiq
  class Rails < ::Rails::Engine
    class Reloader
      def initialize(app = ::Rails.application)
        @app = app
      end

      def call
        @app.reloader.wrap do
          yield
        end
      end

      def inspect
        "#<Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader @app=#{@app.class.name}>"
      end
    end

    # By including the Options module, we allow AJs to directly control sidekiq features
    # via the *sidekiq_options* class method and, for instance, not use AJ's retry system.
    # AJ retries don't show up in the Sidekiq UI Retries tab, save any error data, can't be
    # manually retried, don't automatically die, etc.
    #
    #   class SomeJob < ActiveJob::Base
    #     queue_as :default
    #     sidekiq_options retry: 3, backtrace: 10
    #     def perform
    #     end
    #   end
    initializer "sidekiq.active_job_integration" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        include ::Sidekiq::Job::Options unless respond_to?(:sidekiq_options)
      end
    end

    config.before_configuration do
      dep = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("7.0", "Sidekiq")
      dep.deprecate_methods(Sidekiq.singleton_class,
        default_worker_options: :default_job_options,
        "default_worker_options=": :default_job_options=)
    end

    # This hook happens after all initializers are run, just before returning
    # from config/environment.rb back to sidekiq/cli.rb.
    #
    # None of this matters on the client-side, only within the Sidekiq process itself.
    config.after_initialize do
      Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
        config[:reloader] = Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader.new

        # This is the integration code necessary so that if a job uses `Rails.logger.info "Hello"`,
        # it will appear in the Sidekiq console with all of the job context.
        unless ::Rails.logger == config.logger || ::ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(::Rails.logger, $stdout)
          if ::Rails::VERSION::STRING < "7.1"
            ::Rails.logger.extend(::ActiveSupport::Logger.broadcast(config.logger))
          else
            ::Rails.logger.broadcast_to(config.logger)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

def serialize_argument(argument) # :nodoc:
      case argument
      when nil, true, false, Integer, Float # Types that can hardly be subclassed
        argument
      when String
        if argument.class == String
          argument
        else
          begin
            Serializers.serialize(argument)
          rescue SerializationError
            argument
          end
        end
      when Symbol
        { OBJECT_SERIALIZER_KEY => "ActiveJob::Serializers::SymbolSerializer", "value" => argument.name }
      when GlobalID::Identification
        convert_to_global_id_hash(argument)
      when Array
        argument.map { |arg| serialize_argument(arg) }
      when ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess
        serialize_indifferent_hash(argument)
      when Hash
        symbol_keys = argument.keys
        symbol_keys.select! { |k| k.is_a?(Symbol) }
        symbol_keys.map!(&:name)

        aj_hash_key = if Hash.ruby2_keywords_hash?(argument)
          RUBY2_KEYWORDS_KEY
        else
          SYMBOL_KEYS_KEY
        end
        result = serialize_hash(argument)
        result[aj_hash_key] = symbol_keys
        result
      else
        Serializers.serialize(argument)
      end

def deserialize(argument)
        serializer_name = argument[Arguments::OBJECT_SERIALIZER_KEY]
        raise ArgumentError, "Serializer name is not present in the argument: #{argument.inspect}" unless serializer_name

        serializer = serializer_name.safe_constantize
        raise ArgumentError, "Serializer #{serializer_name} is not known" unless serializer

        serializer.deserialize(argument)
      end

# This is to avoid ActiveModel (and by extension the entire framework)
        # being dependent on a binary library.
        begin
          require "bcrypt"
        rescue LoadError
          warn "You don't have bcrypt installed in your application. Please add it to your Gemfile and run bundle install."
          raise
        end

        include InstanceMethodsOnActivation.new(attribute, reset_token: reset_token)

        if validations
          include ActiveModel::Validations

          # This ensures the model has a password by checking whether the password_digest
          # is present, so that this works with both new and existing records. However,
          # when there is an error, the message is added to the password attribute instead
          # so that the error message will make sense to the end-user.
          validate do |record|
            record.errors.add(attribute, :blank) unless record.public_send("#{attribute}_digest").present?
          end

          validate do |record|
            if challenge = record.public_send(:"#{attribute}_challenge")
              digest_was = record.public_send(:"#{attribute}_digest_was") if record.respond_to?(:"#{attribute}_digest_was")

              unless digest_was.present? && BCrypt::Password.new(digest_was).is_password?(challenge)
                record.errors.add(:"#{attribute}_challenge")
              end
            end
          end

          # Validates that the password does not exceed the maximum allowed bytes for BCrypt (72 bytes).
          validate do |record|
            password_value = record.public_send(attribute)
            if password_value.present? && password_value.bytesize > ActiveModel::SecurePassword::MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH_ALLOWED
              record.errors.add(attribute, :password_too_long)
            end
          end

          validates_confirmation_of attribute, allow_nil: true
        end

content.text:
I found 20 changes between 7.0.8.7 and 8.1.0 that affect Margin Notes: 9 high, 4 medium and 7 low. Most of them come from 7.2 and 8.0, not 8.1 itself. Many of the high-risk ones fail silently in production, but the existing tests should fail on most of them. Nothing was installed, run or changed in the app. I compared the released gems, unpacked under `/tmp/railsdiff/src/{7.0.8.7,8.1.0}/<gem>`, using the changelogs from 7.1.5.2, 7.2.2.2 and 8.0.3 (all in that same folder). I couldn't look up PR numbers because the GitHub API was rate-limited, so the links below go to the changelog files. Sources are marked **[changelog]**, **[code]** (Rails or app source I read) or **[inference]**.

## Facts the ratings depend on (please correct any that are wrong)
- **Framework defaults stay at 7.0** (`/home/user/workspace/repo/config/application.rb:12`). Many behavior changes from 7.1 to 8.1 only apply after you raise that setting, so they are not counted here. There's a short list of them at the end. [code]
- **Database:** PostgreSQL through `pg` 1.6.0. MySQL and SQLite changes don't apply. [code]
- **Background jobs:** Active Job uses Rails' built-in Sidekiq adapter, with Sidekiq 6.5.12 and redis 4.8.1 (`config/application.rb:24`); tests use the `:test` adapter. `ExportJob` is a plain Sidekiq job, so Active Job changes don't touch it. [code]
- **Rolling deploys:** I assumed web and worker processes can briefly run different Rails versions during a deploy, and that reminder jobs may be scheduled weeks ahead. [inference]
- **Front end:** the app renders HTML with Sprockets and importmap. It loads a vendored Trix 1.3.5 as a plain script and uses Action Text and Active Storage on local disk. It serves no JSON. [code]
- **Caching:** the only caching is one fragment cache in the exports page. Production sets no cache store, so Rails' default file store applies. [code/inference]
- **Settings:** citation-provider settings come from `config/secrets.yml` through `Rails.application.secrets`. [code]
- **Unused frameworks:** Action Cable has no channels and Action Mailbox isn't used. [code]
- **Tests:** there are no system (browser) tests, so editor and styling changes are untested. [code]
- **Ruby:** 3.3.6, and Rails 8.1 needs 3.2 or later. [code]
- **Dependencies:** 8.1 adds `action_text-trix`, `useragent`, `rack-session` and `rackup` to the bundle. Nothing in 8.1 forces a change to the pinned Sidekiq, redis, rack, concurrent-ruby or minitest versions. [code: 8.1.0 gem metadata]

## High risk (behavior changes without an error)

**1. `return` inside a transaction now commits instead of rolling back.** Removed in 7.2 ([7-2-stable AR changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md): "Remove deprecated behavior that would rollback a transaction block when exited using `return`..."; background in [7-1-stable](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md)). [changelog + code]
- **Before:** 7.0's `within_new_transaction` rolled back when the block exited early after writing.
- **Now:** 8.1 commits whenever no exception was raised.
- **Where:** `Import#apply` in `/home/user/workspace/repo/app/models/import.rb:53-58` does `return false unless row.note.save` inside `transaction`.
- **What breaks:** an import with a bad row would keep the Import, every note before the bad row and any new citations. The page still says "Nothing has been saved." The fix is to raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback` or call `save!` and rescue. `test/controllers/imports_controller_test.rb:65-72` should catch it. [inference]

**2. Times passed to jobs now arrive in the reader's time zone, not UTC.** Changed in 7.2 ([7-2-stable activejob](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md): "Preserve the serialized timezone when deserializing `ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone` arguments"). [changelog + code]
- **Before:** 7.0 rebuilt the time in the worker's zone, UTC.
- **Now:** 8.1 also stores the zone name and restores it (`time_with_zone_serializer.rb`).
- **Where:** `User#request_digest` passes the time in the reader's zone (`app/models/user.rb:35,41`). `DigestMailer` (`app/mailers/digest_mailer.rb:8-9`) uses `requested_at.to_date` and `requested_at.all_day`.
- **What breaks:** the digest silently switches to the reader's local day. The Redis reservation key is still the UTC day (`user.rb:36`), so near local midnight the two disagree, which contradicts the docs. `test/controllers/digests_controller_test.rb:33` (subject date) should fail. [inference]

**3. Digest jobs fail while old and new versions run side by side.** 7.2 removed the old way of passing `BigDecimal` arguments, and 8.0 removed the setting that controlled it ([7-2-stable activejob](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md), [8-0-stable activejob](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md)). [changelog + code]
- **Change:** 8.1 always wraps `BigDecimal` as `ActiveJob::Serializers::BigDecimalSerializer`.
- **Where:** `user.rb:41` passes the reading-completion share as a `BigDecimal`.
- **What breaks:**
  - A 7.0 worker can't find that serializer class, so it raises an error while reading the job's arguments (`DeserializationError`).
  - `DigestJob` has no `discard_on`, so Sidekiq keeps retrying until a new worker picks it up.
  - Meanwhile the reader's Redis reservation blocks them from asking again that day.
- **Other direction:** 7.0-enqueued jobs run fine on 8.1. The completion value arrives as a string and `BigDecimal()` accepts it, the time falls back to UTC, and scheduled `NoteReminderJob`s keep the same wrapper class name. [code]

**4. The import receipt CSV loses its DOI column.** Removed in 7.2 ([7-2-stable AR](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md): "Remove deprecated support to `ActiveRecord::Base#read_attribute(:id)` to return the custom primary key value"). [changelog + code]
- **Before:** in 7.0, `record[:id]` returned the primary key even when it isn't `id`.
- **Now:** 8.1 reads a column literally named `id`. `citations` has none (its primary key is `doi`), so it silently returns `nil`.
- **Where:** `Import#receipt` uses `citation && citation[:id]` (`app/models/import.rb:68`).
- **What breaks:** every DOI cell in the downloaded receipt is blank. Use `citation.doi`. `imports_controller_test.rb:43-45` should catch it. [inference]

**5. Annotations disappear from the import preview.** Changed in 8.0 ([8-0-stable activesupport](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md): "Fix `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess#stringify_keys` to stringify all keys not just symbols"). [changelog + code]
- **Where:** `/home/user/workspace/repo/app/views/imports/preview.html.erb:22` calls `@import.annotations.stringify_keys`. That hash is keyed by integer line numbers, and line 42 looks them up with `annotations[row.line]`.
- **Before:** in 7.0, `stringify_keys` left integer keys alone.
- **Now:** keys become `"2"`, so the lookup returns `nil` and annotations vanish from the preview without an error. `imports_controller_test.rb:22,24` should fail. [inference]

**6. The "24 hours later" reminder preview shows a different local time and offset.** 8.0 added the `:zone` behavior and 8.1 removed the old modes ([8-0-stable activesupport](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md), [v8.1.0 activesupport](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md): "Remove deprecated support for `to_time` to preserve the system local time..."). [changelog + code]
- **Before:** 7.0 defaults kept a fixed offset.
- **Now:** in 8.1, `TimeWithZone#to_time` always keeps the zone (`getlocal(time_zone)`).
- **Where:** `Note#next_day_reminder_at` (`app/models/note.rb:43-45`), shown in `app/views/notes/_reminder.html.erb:19`.
- **What changes:** across a daylight-saving change the preview now shows the zone's new offset and local time. The moment is the same, and so is the `.to_i` value used for postponing. This arguably fixes what ARCHITECTURE.md describes as a known oddity, so the docs need updating. `test/controllers/reminders_controller_test.rb:21` asserts the old value. [inference]

**7. Readers whose time zone is "Astana" shift by an hour.** Changed in 7.2 ([7-2-stable activesupport](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md): "Updating Astana with Western Kazakhstan TZInfo identifier"). [changelog + code]
- **Change:** "Astana" now maps to `Asia/Almaty` instead of `Asia/Dhaka`.
- **Where:** a reader's stored zone name drives reminder display (`note.rb:37`) and how entered times are read (`user.rb:22`). [code]
- **Not affected:** the zone names `User` validates against are unchanged apart from a new "Asuncion", and the "Greenland" and "Canberra" remaps point to equivalent zones.
- **What changes:** with current tz data, Astana readers see reminder times an hour different, and newly entered times land an hour apart. [inference]

**8. Markdown export text changes for some notes.** This comes from the code diff of `plain_text_conversion.rb`; it isn't in the changelog. [code]
- **Lists:** numbered-list items are now counted by element only. Before, whitespace between `<li>` tags also counted, so imported HTML produced "2., 4.". [code]
- **Script and style:** `<script>` and `<style>` content is now dropped. [code]
- **Where:** `Export#markdown_for` (`app/models/export.rb:78`) and the note list excerpt (`app/views/notes/index.html.erb:53`). Mostly HTML imported through `body_html`. [inference]

**9. Expired export fragments are now cached forever, and an error is logged.** Changed in 7.1. [code]
- **Before:** in 7.0, a negative `expires_in` stored an entry that expired immediately.
- **Now:** in 8.1, `merged_options` drops a negative `expires_in`, logs an `ArgumentError` and stores the entry with no expiry. That's because `raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time` stays false under 7.0 defaults.
- **Where:** `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26` uses `expires_in: export.expires_at - Time.current`, which is negative once an export has expired.
- **Impact:** the cached content ("Expired") is still correct, so this mostly means log noise and permanent file-store entries. The tests won't notice. [inference]

## Medium risk (raises an error, and the fix needs a decision)

**10. `Rails.application.secrets` was removed.** Deprecated in 7.1, removed in 7.2 ([7-2-stable railties](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/railties/CHANGELOG.md)). [changelog + code]
- **Where:** `/home/user/workspace/repo/app/models/citation/provider.rb:13`, plus test stubbing at `test/controllers/citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:45,117-122`.
- **When it fails:** boot is fine. It raises `NoMethodError` when a `CitationEnrichmentJob` runs. That isn't the `Unavailable` error the job retries on, so Sidekiq keeps retrying and the citation stays "pending" (which also blocks re-requests).
- **Decision:** move these settings to credentials, `config_for`, or plain environment variables. [inference]

**11. The Action Text allowlist initializer crashes at boot.** [code]
- **Before:** in 7.0, `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags` defaulted to a list.
- **Now:** in 8.1 it is `nil`, and the default list is built in `sanitizer_allowed_tags`.
- **Where:** `/home/user/workspace/repo/config/initializers/action_text.rb:3` does `nil += %w[details summary]`, which raises `NoMethodError` at boot.
- **Decision:** rebuild the whole list: sanitizer defaults, the attachment tag, `figure`, `figcaption`, plus `details` and `summary`. Setting only `details` and `summary` would silently strip everything else from rich text.

**12. Trix moved to its own gem, so the editor's CSS no longer matches its JavaScript.** From the [v8.1.0 actiontext changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md) ("satisfied by a gem, `action_text-trix`... upgrades Trix to `>= 2.1.15`"). [changelog + code]
- **Change:** `*= require trix` in `app/assets/stylesheets/actiontext.css:6` now pulls Trix 2.1.15 CSS from the new gem. The layout still loads the vendored Trix 1.3.5 JavaScript (`app/views/layouts/application.html.erb:13`).
- **What still works:** `actiontext.js` (`config/importmap.rb:8`) still loads as a module and still uses Trix 1-compatible upload calls.
- **Decision:** keep Trix 1.3.5 and vendor its CSS, or move to Trix 2 and drop the workaround. The reason for the workaround (7.0 bundling Trix 1.3.4) no longer applies. No test covers the editor. [inference]

**13. The built-in Sidekiq adapter is deprecated and goes away in Rails 8.2.** From the [v8.1.0 activejob changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/activejob/CHANGELOG.md). [changelog + code]
- **8.1:** it only warns. Production hides deprecations (`config/environments/production.rb:76`).
- **Replacement:** Sidekiq 7.3.3 or later. That moves off redis-rb 4, so check `Sidekiq.redis { |r| r.sadd ... }` truthiness at `app/models/user.rb:38` and `rescue Redis::BaseError` at `app/models/notebook.rb:28`. [inference]
- **Compatibility:** Sidekiq 6.5.12's own Rails integration supports 7.1+ logging and should work with 8.1. [code + inference]

## Low risk (mechanical; booting or the tests would catch it)
14. **`serialize :tags, JSON`** (`app/models/note.rb:12`) is removed syntax and raises `ArgumentError` at load. Use `coder: JSON`. [changelog 7.2 + code]
15. **`enum status: {...}, _prefix: true`** (`note.rb:10`) is removed syntax. Use `enum :status, {...}, prefix: true`. [changelog 8.0 + code]
16. **`alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color`** (`note.rb:14`) points at a `store_accessor`, not a real attribute, and raises `ArgumentError` when the first Note loads. Use `alias_method` for both the reader and the writer. [changelog 7.2 + code]
17. **`retry_on ..., wait: :exponentially_longer`** (`app/jobs/citation_enrichment_job.rb:7`): the option was removed. It fails only when a retry happens ("Couldn't determine a delay"), not at boot. Rename to `:polynomially_longer` (same formula). The test at `citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:60-71` exercises retries. [changelog 7.2 + code]
18. **`set(wait_until: reminder_epoch)` with an Integer** (`note.rb:61`): job serialization calls `.utc` on it and raises inside `with_lock`. Use `Time.at(reminder_epoch)`. [changelog 7.2 + code]
19. **`form_with(model: nil, ...)`** (`app/views/notes/index.html.erb:12`) now raises `ArgumentError` on the main notes page. Drop `model: nil`. [changelog 8.0 + code]
20. **Other mechanical changes:**
    - **`where(notebooks: @notebook)`** (`app/controllers/notes_controller.rb:12`): the plural fallback was removed, so this becomes the column `notes.notebooks` and SQL fails. Use `notebook:`. [changelog 7.2 + code]
    - **`get "/notes", "/journal", to:`** (`config/routes.rb:18`): one path per call now; it raises at boot. [changelog 8.0/8.1 + code]
    - **`show_exceptions = false`** (`config/environments/test.rb:31`): 8.1 treats `false` as "show all", so every `assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)` test fails. Use `:none`. [changelog 7.2 + code]
    - **`db/schema.rb`:** the next dump will list columns alphabetically, so expect a noisy diff. [changelog 8.1]
    - **Updated timestamps:** since 7.1, analyzing an Active Storage blob touches the records it's attached to. That moves `updated_at` on exports and on notes with attachments, which `DigestMailer` filters on. The effect should be tiny. [changelog 7.1 + inference]

## Not relevant here
- **Jobs queued inside a transaction:** `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` defaults to `false` in 8.1 (`enqueuing.rb:53`), so jobs queued under `with_lock` (`citation.rb:15-22`, `note.rb:57-63`) still go out immediately. If you deploy 7.2 as a stop on the way, they would be deferred until commit. [code + changelog]
- **Sessions and cookies:** with 7.0 defaults, the JSON cookie serializer and SHA256 key derivation are unchanged, so existing sessions survive. The production `secret_key_base` must come from an environment variable or credentials, because `secrets.yml` no longer works. [code + inference]
